gaps.sentence: All the tickets ___ (sell) within an hour of going on sale.
gaps.explanation: Past simple passive: were + sold. 'All the tickets' takes a plural verb.

gaps.sentence: The two leaders ___ (report) to have reached a provisional agreement.
gaps.explanation: Plural subject needs are: are reported to have reached (perfect infinitive for the earlier event).

gaps.sentence: Historic documents ___ (digitise) right now, which is why the archive is shut.
gaps.hint: action in progress now, plural subject
gaps.explanation: Present continuous passive: are being + digitised for an action happening around now.

gaps.sentence: Your booking ___ (confirm) by email — check your spam folder.
gaps.explanation: Present perfect passive: has been + confirmed; the confirmation exists now.

gaps.sentence: The stairs ___ (reinforce) when part of the ceiling gave way.
gaps.hint: action in progress at a past moment
gaps.explanation: Past continuous passive: was/were being + past participle, interrupted by a sudden past event.

gaps.sentence: The new bridge ___ (open) by the mayor next month.
gaps.explanation: Future simple passive: will be + opened, with the agent in a by-phrase.

gaps.sentence: By this time tomorrow, the results ___ to every candidate.
gaps.explanation: 'By this time tomorrow' requires future perfect passive: will have been + emailed.

gaps.sentence: The evidence ___ by an independent laboratory at present.
gaps.explanation: 'At present' needs present continuous passive: is being + analysed. The lab does the analysing.
